context: You are a member of a fitness club. You received an email from the manager of the club.

paragraphs: I am sorry to inform you that the fitness centre is closing for a month from next Monday. The building needs some repairs and we also plan to install some new equipment.

What else do you think should be changed? As the centre will not be operating for a month, what kind of alternative activities should we organise in the meantime? We appreciate your opinion very much.

task11: Write a letter to your friend, who is also a member of the club. Write about your feelings and what you think the club management should do about the situation.
task12: Write a letter to the manager. Write about your feelings and what you think the club management should do about the situation.
part2_question: Is it better to live in a big city or a small town?

task11: Have you read the manager's email? The club is closing for a whole month. I am quite disappointed, because I train there three times a week. I think they should run outdoor sessions in the park so that we keep our routine. Would you come to those?
task12: Thank you for telling us about the temporary closure of the fitness centre. I understand that the repairs and the new equipment are necessary, but I must admit that I am disappointed, as training here is an important part of my week.

You asked what else should change. In my opinion, the changing rooms need attention most: they are small and often untidy. I would also welcome more classes in the evening, when most members are free. A few members have also mentioned that the equipment in the free-weights area is often left untidy.
As for the closing month, outdoor group sessions in the park or online training videos would keep us motivated. Regular updates on the progress of the work would also be appreciated.
part2: Both big cities and small towns have their attractions, but on balance I believe a big city offers more for someone at the start of their career.

The first reason is opportunity. Cities contain far more employers, and a person working in a specialised field has a realistic chance of finding the right job. Someone interested in technology, for example, will find many more openings in a city than in a provincial town.

The second reason is variety. Museums, theatres, concerts and restaurants from a dozen countries are all within reach, and this constant contact with different cultures broadens the way you think. A city also exposes you to ideas and people you would simply never meet at home.

Of course, city life has a price. Housing is expensive, the streets are noisy and the pace can be exhausting, whereas a small town offers calm and a genuine sense of community. Many people also find that neighbours in a small town know and help one another in a way that rarely happens in a city block.
In the end the choice depends on your stage of life, but for those seeking growth, the city is usually the better option.
